did_you_know.text: Did you know? Gog is described as the “chief prince of Meshech and Tubal,” and a direct prophecy from the LORD is spoken to him.
Did you know? Gog and his armies are led from the “remote parts of the north” to the mountains of Israel as part of the divine plan described in the prophecy.
Did you know? After Gog’s defeat, he, all his forces, and the nations with him are given to the birds of prey and the wild animals as food.
Did you know? Alongside Gog’s defeat, the prophecy also mentions fire being sent against the land of Magog and the people living securely on the islands.
Did you know? The chapter emphasizes that these events will take place on the day spoken of by the LORD, linking their fulfillment to His word and faithfulness.
Did you know? The inhabitants of Israel’s cities will use the weapons left behind by Gog’s army as fuel for seven years, so they will not need to gather wood from the fields or forests.
Did you know? The place where Gog and his armies are buried is called the “Valley of the Multitude of Gog”; according to the text, the valley even blocks the way of travelers.
Did you know? The house of Israel will bury Gog’s multitude for seven months, and the burials will be intended to cleanse the land.
Did you know? After the seven months of burial, designated men will work throughout the land to locate the remains that are left and cleanse it.
Did you know? The prophet commands the birds and wild animals to gather for a “great sacrifice” on the mountains of Israel; this description symbolically portrays the defeat of Gog’s armies.
Did you know? The chapter presents Gog’s defeat and Israel’s restoration as part of a process through which the house of Israel will know the LORD as their God from that day onward.

Did you know? According to the prophecy, the nations will understand that Israel went into exile because of its iniquity and unfaithfulness to the LORD, not because the LORD was unable to protect them.
Did you know? The LORD promises to restore Jacob, have compassion on all the house of Israel, and be zealous for His holy name.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it says that the LORD will no longer hide His face from Israel after pouring out His Spirit on the house of Israel.
